D: A troubled boy befriends a captive orca at an amusement park and sets out to free him.
P: Serve the dessert when Willy jumps over the breakwater.
S: Salmon pieces glazed with soy, honey and ginger, baked at 200C for 10 minutes, served on toothpicks with a lime wedge.

Creamy clam chowder with bacon, potato, onion and thyme, ladled into small cups and topped with crumbled bacon, chives and oyster crackers. Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp and set half aside. Soften an onion and 2 celery sticks in the fat, stir in 2 tbsp flour, then add 2 cans baby clams with their juice, 400ml milk, 2 diced potatoes and thyme. Simmer 15 minutes until the potato is tender. Stir in 150ml cream and heat through without boiling. Ladle into cups and top with bacon, chives and oyster crackers.
Glen and Annie's grilled cheese soldiers
Buttery toasted cheddar sandwiches fried golden in the pan and cut into fingers for dipping in tomato sauce.
M: Pacific Northwest, out by the water

Linguine tossed with sweet crab meat, garlic, a little chilli, lemon zest and parsley in good olive oil, finished with toasted breadcrumbs. Cook 400g linguine in well salted water. Toast 40g breadcrumbs in a little oil until golden. Gently fry 3 sliced garlic cloves and half a seeded red chilli in 80ml olive oil for 2 minutes. Add 300g crab meat, the zest and juice of a lemon and a ladle of pasta water and warm through. Toss with the drained pasta and chopped parsley, then scatter with the crumbs.
the night drive to get Willy to the sea

White fish strips crumbed in panko and fried crisp, tucked into warm tortillas with lime slaw, sliced avocado and a lime and sour cream crema. Cut 600g flathead fillets into strips. Dust in flour, dip in 2 beaten eggs and coat in 100g panko. Fry at 180C for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Toss a quarter cabbage, shredded, with lime juice and salt. Mix 150g sour cream with lime zest and juice. Warm 8 flour tortillas and fill with slaw, fish, sliced avocado and crema.
W: Vanilla ice cream churned with crushed chocolate cream biscuits, scooped into bowls with a little white chocolate fin on top.
K: Willy back in the open ocean
Lemonade with a few drops of blue colouring and a scoop of vanilla ice cream floating on top, served in tall glasses.

s.how: Cut 600g salmon fillet into bite-sized cubes. Mix 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey and grated ginger and toss the salmon through. Spread on a lined tray and bake at 200C for 10 minutes until just cooked and sticky. Spear on toothpicks and serve with lime wedges.

s.n: Glen and Annie's grilled cheese soldiers
s.how: Butter 8 slices of bread on the outside and sandwich with 8 slices cheddar. Cook in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden and melted. Cut each sandwich into 4 fingers and serve warm with tomato sauce for dipping.

m.note: Pacific Northwest, out by the water
m.how: Cook 400g linguine in well salted water. Toast 40g breadcrumbs in a little oil until golden. Gently fry 3 sliced garlic cloves and half a seeded red chilli in 80ml olive oil for 2 minutes. Add 300g crab meat, the zest and juice of a lemon and a ladle of pasta water and warm through. Toss with the drained pasta and chopped parsley, then scatter with the crumbs.

w.how: Soften 1L vanilla ice cream slightly and fold through 150g crushed chocolate cream biscuits. Refreeze for 2 hours. Melt white chocolate, pipe little fin shapes onto baking paper and set in the fridge. Scoop the ice cream into bowls and stand a fin on top.

d.note: Willy back in the open ocean
d.how: Pour cold lemonade into tall glasses and add a drop or two of blue food colouring to each, stirring until ocean blue. Gently add a scoop of vanilla ice cream so it floats and foams up. Serve straight away with a long spoon and a straw.
